collection.description: The elders have called a meeting.

ask.text:
There are two people in the village with the same first name, and it has finally caused a disaster: (subject)'s fish order went to (friend), (friend)'s love note went to (subject), and the healers nearly gave (subject) a remedy meant for (friend)'s rash.
The elders have called a meeting. Someone will have to change their name, and (subject), being younger, is expected to offer. (subject) loves (subject.his/her) name. But (subject.he/she) also doesn't want anyone getting the wrong remedy.
What should (subject) do?

c1o1.text: "(renamed)," says an elder, firmly, over the noise. "The name of the earliest riser I ever knew. You've always liked to be up early too." (subject) tries it out, and finds it fits. The village throws a small naming feast, and (friend) gives (subject.him/her) back the love note, which was very embarrassing for everyone.

c1o2.text: There are so many suggestions that in the end they write them all on leaves and put them in a bowl, and (subject) pulls one out without looking. It's an ordinary sort of name. "That'll do," says (subject). By the end of the month (subject.he/she) can't imagine being called anything else.

c1.text: (subject) stands up in the meeting and says (subject.he/she) will change. Everyone looks relieved, and then everyone starts suggesting names at once...

c2o1.text: It works, more or less. The village gets used to adding a little bit to each name, and the deliveries mostly go to the right place. (subject), who was afraid of having to change, feels so relieved that it changes (subject.his/her) mood about other things too. (subject.He/She) used to keep away from village gatherings in case someone called the wrong name; now (subject.he/she) comes to every one.

c2o2.text: It doesn't work. The village can't remember which one is the tall one, and (friend) gets a goat (friend.he/she) didn't ask for. In the end, both of them just learn to check, every time. "Which one?" they ask, whenever anyone calls their name. It becomes a sort of village joke.

c2.text: "Why don't we just call us something different?" (subject) says. "Like 'the tall one' and 'the one with the goat'?" The elders look at each other...
